The *Sakkāra Sutta* (Ud 2.4; PTS Ud 12) is the fourth discourse in the second chapter (Mucalindavagga) of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. The discourse addresses how one should deal with abusive language and contempt [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies verse parallels to the sutta in the "Sukhavarga" (chapter on happiness) of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 30; UVS 30), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 30), and Chinese collections (*Chūyào jīng*, T 212.31; *Fǎjí yàosòng jīng*, T 213.30) [SuttaCentral].
